discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC through the conception, construction and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but not the experimental achievement that confirmed it. The 2012 observation of a new scalar boson near 125 GeV required general-purpose detectors of unprecedented complexity, conceived in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson) and Michel Della Negra (founding CMS spokesperson) led the design and construction of these instruments. Fabiola Gianotti led ATLAS through the discovery and the careful control of systematics that made the 5-sigma claim credible. Since then, the two experiments have established the particle's spin-parity and its couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and now muons. They have also opened the first direct access to Higgs pair production and the shape of the Higgs potential. This is the only elementary scalar known in nature, and its discovery completed the Standard Model.
